system.devWarningBody:
WARNING: Developer Mode enables development and diagnostic tools that can expose or change sensitive system state.

Developer Mode does not by itself disable the app sandbox or grant every app unrestricted filesystem, network, or system access. Tools and actions remain subject to their own permission checks. Use these capabilities only on a device you trust.

Developer Mode also makes it possible to enable Root Access in Settings. Root Access is a separate device-wide switch, and each app still needs its own explicit grant. A root-approved app runs directly inside the OS page without a sandbox and can read or change system data and UI. Only grant it to apps you fully trust.

Developer Mode is intended for development, debugging, and system maintenance. Enable it only when needed, and leave it disabled during normal use.

root.intro: Root apps run directly in the OS page with unrestricted access and can perform real administrator (root) operations. Every root app first asks for your confirmation inside a NovaByte prompt — never inside the app — and every privileged operation runs through audited, passwordless sudo (NOPASSWD) and is written to the security log. This is not a sandbox or a normal app permission.

appmanager.impersonationBody: declares itself a NovaByte System package but does not hold a valid, matching System signature and intact contents.
appmanager.impersonationWhyTitle: Why this is blocked, not just a warning
appmanager.impersonationWhyBody: A real NovaByte System package has no legitimate reason to fail signature or integrity verification. This combination — claiming the System badge while failing that check — is a defining sign of an attempt to impersonate a trusted system component rather than an ordinary publishing mistake. NovaByte OS does not offer an override for this case.
appmanager.integrityFailed: ⚠️ failed — contents do not match build-time hash
appmanager.integrityUnavailable: not available — package has no integrity hash to check against
appmanager.untrustedRevokedSummary: carries a signature that has been individually revoked by NovaByte OS. This package was previously verified as signed by a trusted authority, but was subsequently pulled from the trust list — most likely because it was found to be harmful, deceptive, or non-compliant after review.
appmanager.untrustedRevokedCaution: A revoked signature means NovaByte OS once recognised the publisher, but has since decided this specific package should not be trusted. Other packages from the same publisher may still be trusted, but this one is not. Installing it bypasses an explicit security decision.
appmanager.untrustedUnknownSummary: is signed, but the signer is not in NovaByte OS's trust store. This usually means the app is self-signed by an individual developer, or signed by an authority that hasn't been reviewed and added to the system trust list.
appmanager.untrustedUnknownCaution: NovaByte OS cannot confirm the identity of the publisher or guarantee that the package has not been modified since it was signed. This doesn't prove the app is malicious — it just means nobody vetted the publisher on your behalf. Proceed only if you obtained the package directly from a developer or source you personally trust.
appmanager.untrustedUnsignedSummary: is not digitally signed. NovaByte OS cannot verify who created the package, when it was built, or whether it has been altered since distribution.
appmanager.untrustedUnsignedCaution: An unsigned package provides no cryptographic proof of origin. Anyone could have created or modified it. Only proceed if you inspected the package yourself and trust its source completely.
appmanager.sigRevoked: present, but revoked by NovaByte OS
appmanager.sigUnrecognised: present, but not from a recognised signer
appmanager.revocationReasonValue: Removed from trust list by NovaByte OS
appmanager.moreInfoTrustNote: Only install or run apps obtained from sources you trust. A missing or unrecognised signature means NovaByte OS cannot confirm who published this app or guarantee it has not been modified since distribution.
appmanager.moreInfoRevokedNote: A revoked signature means NovaByte OS reviewed this package and explicitly decided it should no longer be trusted — installing it overrides that decision.
appmanager.moreInfoFooter: If you do not trust the source, cancel this operation and remove the package.
appmanager.tamperSummary: failed its integrity check. The package's contents no longer match the hash that was recorded when it was built. This is true regardless of whether the package is signed by a trusted publisher — a valid signature only proves who signed the original file, not that these are still its unmodified contents.
appmanager.tamperWhyBody: A mismatch here usually means the file was altered after it was packaged — by corruption in transit, or by someone modifying it deliberately. NovaByte OS cannot tell which. Installing this package means running code that is provably different from what its integrity hash says it should be.
appmanager.maliciousDefaultReason: It matched a pattern associated with malicious files.
appmanager.maliciousSummary: was blocked before install. This application may cause damage to your device, steal data, or behave in ways you didn't authorize — installation cannot continue.
appmanager.maliciousHeuristicNote: This scan is a heuristic check, not a full antivirus — it looks for known red flags like disguised executables, hidden scripts inside files that shouldn't have any, and obfuscated or packed code. A block here means something concrete tripped that check. If you trust the source and believe this is a false positive, get an updated package from the publisher rather than forcing this one through — NovaByte OS won't install a file that fails this check.
appmanager.comboRevokedSummary: This package's signature was individually revoked by NovaByte OS — it was previously trusted, but has since been pulled from the trust list, most likely because it was found to be harmful, deceptive, or non-compliant after review.
appmanager.comboUnknownSummary: This package is signed, but the signer is not in NovaByte OS's trust store. NovaByte OS cannot confirm the identity of the publisher.
appmanager.comboUnsignedSummary: This package is not digitally signed. NovaByte OS cannot verify who created it or whether it has been altered since distribution.
appmanager.comboSummary: failed two independent checks: NovaByte OS cannot confirm who published it, and its contents no longer match the hash recorded at build time. These are separate risks — either one alone would be worth pausing on; together, proceed only if you're certain of both the source and the copy you have.
appmanager.comboIntegrityBody: The package's contents no longer match the hash recorded when it was built. This is true regardless of who signed it — a valid signature only proves who signed the original file, not that these are still its unmodified contents.
